subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a static vehicle model as a single TypeScript module, aiming for around 200 parts built with the b.part builder using positions, directions, and aim targets, favoring simple geometries like cylinders for wheels to keep the risky, untestable API usage manageable.

The design is an armored truck roughly 9m long, 3m wide, 3.4m tall, facing +Z, with six wheels across three axles, a wedge-shaped cab, cargo bed with container modules, roof-mounted turret, glowing neon strips and headlights, antenna, sensor dome, armor plating, exhaust stacks, and fuel tanks, using helper functions for boxes and cylinders plus a glow kit import, with a color palette of gunmetal hull, dark olive armor, hazard yellow accents, and cyan/magenta/orange neon highlights.

Now I'm working out precise coordinates: ground at y=0, wheels radius 0.7 centered at y=0.7, axles spaced along z (front ~3.0, mid ~-0.6, rear ~-2.2), chassis rails at y 1.1–1.4 with width ±0.8, and deck at y 1.5. For the cab, I'm placing the body box around z 1.6–4.0 and y 1.5–3.0, adding a sloped hood and windshield using rotated boxes, a roof plate, and side window slits, while confirming the rotation convention tilts boxes about the X axis to angle them toward the front.

Now I'm detailing the wheels with tire cylinders and hub caps, lug bolt rings, fenders, and mud flaps, adjusting wheel offset and width so the outer tire edge stays within the body's half-width. I'm also laying out the cargo bed deck dimensions and planning stacked container modules with panel lines, hazard stripes, vents, and a tilted missile launcher pod with six tubes on top.

Adding more vehicle details...

Mirroring the right-side emblem should keep the text readable. Now I'm adding fine details like panel seams, rivets, cage armor over windows, roof light pods, and vent grills, then setting up helper functions for boxes, cylinders, and glow effects to streamline the build.

I'm checking the tire bottom sits flush at ground level and laying out the axle positions along the z-axis—front axle, two rear axles, bed, and cab—to total about 9.1 units of length, then writing the full vehicle construction loop.

Writing vehicle geometry...

Adding roof plate, side window slits with dark cyan glow, and gunmetal frames, then building the front bumper bull-bar, headlight glow slits, an amber roof light bar, and a slatted grille.

Now I'm positioning side exhaust stacks as vertical cylinders behind the cab with glowing tip rings, and working out cylindrical fuel tank placement along the chassis so they don't collide with the wheel positions.

I'm checking clearances for fenders and skirt armor over the rear wheels, settling on simple arched boxes positioned just above the wheel tops so they don't intersect the tires.

Now I'm laying out the cargo module and missile rack on the bed, deciding to split the rear deck into a container section (roughly z -2.9 to -0.1) and a separate rack base further back (z -4.5 to -3.0) to avoid overlapping volumes.

Working out tilt angles and tube positions for the rack now, with two rows of four tubes angled upward and backward, plus glowing red end caps and a support bracket -- then moving on to design a roof turret on the cab.

Now I'm placing the turret's base cylinder, body box, and twin forward-facing barrels with glowing muzzles, plus a sensor dome, radar dish, and rear antennas. For the container, I'm adding vertical rib strips along the sides, alternating yellow-black hazard stripes along the bottom edge, and a glowing cyan neon strip along the top.

Adding rear tail lights, chassis rails, underglow strips, and axle cylinders with glowing hub caps for the wheels...

I need to match the box rotation angle to the radial direction so the tread sits flush against the tire. I'm trimming part count to about 10 tread blocks per wheel to stay under the limit, and double-checking the tire radius so the tread doesn't poke below the ground plane.

With geometry settled, I'm finalizing the emblem as a small SVG with "OMNI-7 / 2077" text in magenta/cyan, positioning the plane symmetrically on both sides, then writing out the final export code while keeping rotation types consistent and allowing flexible option spreading.
